{"description": "- Document page (first page of an academic journal article), white background, black text, two-column lower layout.
- Top header band: left = Elsevier logo (orange 'ELSEVIER' wordmark beneath a gray tree illustration); center top = small text 'Contents lists available at ScienceDirect'; center = journal title 'Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering'; below title = 'journal homepage: www.elsevier.com/locate/soildyn' (URL in blue); right = blue vertical banner box with white text 'THE CIVIL ENGINEERING ENGINEERS' and a yellow graphic; far right = gray 'CrossMark' logo.
- Article title (large bold): 'Seismic analysis of underground tunnels by the 2.5D finite/infinite element approach'.
- Author line: 'K.C. Lin a, H.H. Hung b, Judy P. Yang c,*, Y.B. Yang d'.
- Affiliation footnotes: 'a Department of Civil Engineering, National Taiwan University, Taipei 10617, Taiwan'; 'b National Center for Research on Earthquake Engineering, Taipei 106, Taiwan'; 'c Department of Civil Engineering, National Chiao Tung University, Hsinchu 30010, Taiwan'; 'd MOE Key Laboratory of New Technology for Construction of Cities in Mountain Area and School of Civil Engineering, Chongqing University, Chongqing 400045, China'.
- Left lower column header 'ARTICLE INFO' (spaced caps) over a horizontal rule; subheader 'Article history:'; lines 'Received 17 December 2015', 'Received in revised form', '9 February 2016', 'Accepted 3 March 2016'; subheader 'Keywords:'; italic list 'Earthquake', 'Free field', 'Infinite element', '2.5D approach', 'Tunnel', 'Wave transmission'.
- Right lower column header 'ABSTRACT' (spaced caps) over a horizontal rule; body text: 'A procedure for the seismic analysis of underground tunnels using recorded free-field earthquakes based on the 2.5D finite/infinite element approach is presented. The near and far fields of the half space are modeled by finite and infinite elements, respectively. Using the 1D wave theory, the nodal force and displacement on the near-field boundary are computed for each spectral frequency of the earthquake. Then, equivalent seismic forces are computed for the near-field boundary for the earthquake spectrum. By assuming the soil-tunnel system to be uniform along the tunnel axis, the 2.5D approach can account for the wave transmission along the tunnel axis, which reduces to the 2D case for infinite transmission velocity. The horizontal and vertical components of the 1999 Chi-Chi Earthquake (TCU068) are adopted as the free-field motions in the numerical analysis. The maximal stresses and distribution patterns of the tunnel section under the P- and SV-waves are thoroughly studied by the 2.5D and 2D approaches, which should prove useful to the design of underground tunnels.'
- Footer bottom right: '© 2016 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved.'
- Spatial layout: header band spans top edge; title and author block centered-left in upper third; affiliations in small italic text below authors; ARTICLE INFO column occupies left ~25% width of lower half, ABSTRACT column occupies right ~75% width of lower half.
- Colors: white page, black body text, orange Elsevier wordmark, blue URL and blue right banner, gray tree/CrossMark, yellow accent in banner.", "image_type": "other"}

{"description": "Scientific diagram on white background illustrating mechanics and chemistry of actuation in a bilayer system. Top center shows a schematic of two stacked rectangles: a gray 'Active layer' above a black 'Passive layer'. Text above reads 'Active layer: modulus E_a, thickness h_a' and 'Actuation strain ε_a^chem due to stimulus driving force ΔE_chem, activation volume Ω'. Two yellow arrows point down at the active layer. Text below reads 'Substrate: modulus E_s, thickness h_s'. Top right box titled 'Energy' shows a curve with a peak labeled 'E_b' and a start point 'E_f', with states 'Contracted state' and 'Expanded state' and energy difference 'ΔE_chem - σ_a Ω'. Formula: 'K_eq = [Expanded state]/[Contracted state] = exp(-(ΔE_chem - σ_a Ω)/kT)'. Bottom center features a large graph with vertical axis 'Actuation stress triggered at surface σ_a' and horizontal axis 'Actuation strain in active layer ε_a^chem', origin marked '0'. A straight line labeled 'σ_a = -ε_a^chem/C_a' descends from top left to bottom right, marked 'Mechanics'. A curve labeled 'σ_a = ΔE_chem/Ω + kT/Ω ln(1 + 3ε_a^chem)' rises from bottom left to top right, marked 'Chemistry (K_eq ≈ 1 + 3ε_a^chem)'. The two lines intersect at a circle in the second quadrant. A box in the bottom right quadrant titled 'Equilibrium:' contains formulas for 'κ', 'α = h_a/h_s', 'β = E_a/E_s', 'φ = ΔE_chem/(3kT)', and 'ω = E_aΩ/(3kT)'.", "image_type": "diagram"}

{"description": "- Asset type: academic research poster, portrait orientation, light blue-gray gradient background.

- Section "Introduction" (blue heading, left column): paragraph on complex microbial communities, biofilms in oral cavity, diamond nanoparticles / nanodiamonds (NDs) as antibacterial agent against planktonic cells (free-floating state); little known about NDs against biofilms (sessile state).

- Center figure panel: (a) grayscale SEM micrograph of nanodiamond crystals, scale bar "500 nm", inset TEM image scale bar "50 nm" and electron diffraction pattern labeled "220", "202", "022", "000"; (b) 2-row schematic: top row "Studying the effects of NDs on biofilm formation" with images labeled "Precoated NDs on substrate" (red text) and "Planktonic cells"; bottom row "Studying the effects of NDs on preformed biofilm" with "Preformed biofilm" (red text) and "NDs solution"; bottom icons labeled "Nanodiamonds (NDs)", cartoon of 3 white teeth in pink gums, and "Biofilm" (brown rods).
